title: 90-Day Planning
subtitle: The planning window that is long enough to matter and short enough to execute
useWhen: Annual plans lose relevance by February. Weekly plans are too reactive to build toward anything significant. You need a planning rhythm that bridges long-term vision and short- term action one that is committed enough to drive behaviour but flexible enough to accommodate reality.
howToUse: The 90-day planning framework, popularised by Michael Watkins in The First 90 Days and widely adopted in the startup and executive world, uses a 13-week window as the fundamental planning unit. Ninety days is long enough to complete a meaningful initiative, short enough to stay relevant, and naturally aligns with quarterly business rhythms. A well- structured 90-day plan has three elements: three Breakthrough Goals (the outcomes that will make this quarter meaningful), Weekly Milestones (the proof that each goal is on track), and a Weekly Review habit (the discipline that closes the loop). The framework fails most often not from picking the wrong goals but from picking too many. Three genuinely completed goals beat seven half-finished ones, and the discipline of saying no to the fourth goal is where most of the real planning work happens.
steps: Choose three Breakthrough Goals not ten. Three that are completed beats ten that are half-done.
Each goal should be uncomfortable to commit to if it feels safe, lower the ambition or pick a different goal.
Build weekly milestones before the quarter starts, if you can't describe progress at week 4, the goal is not specific enough.
Schedule a 30-minute quarterly review on the last day of each 90-day period before starting the next.
origin: Michael Watkins, The First 90 Days, 2003 · Quarterly planning methodology
promptBody:
Act as a 90-day planning coach.
My context                :  [YOUR ROLE, CURRENT BUSINESS STAGE, KEY PRIORITIES]
Longer-term vision :  [WHERE YOU ARE TRYING TO GET TO IN 12–18 MONTHS]
Current blockers      :  [WHAT IS SLOWING YOUR PROGRESS MOST]
Build my 90-Day Plan:
BREAKTHROUGH GOALS :  3 outcomes that would make this quarter genuinely 
                                                   significant  not just busy.
For each: define what done looks like measurably.
WEEKLY MILESTONES    :  For each goal  what should I have achieved by week 4, week 
                                                 8, and week 12?
KEYSTONE HABITS          :  2 weekly behaviours that are preconditions for hitting these  
                                                 goals.
NOT-TO-DO LIST              :  3 things I must stop doing or deprioritise to protect capacity  
                                                 for these goals.
WEEKLY CHECK-IN          :  One question to ask myself every Friday to assess whether
                                                  I am on track.

proTip:
The Not-To-Do List is as important as the goal list. Every 90-Day Plan assumes you will
have capacity you don't currently have. That capacity has to come from somewhere  and
the only honest place it can come from is stopping or delegating something you
currently do. Write the Not-To-Do List before you commit to the goals.
